summary: The script faithfully implements the paper's multi-level dense layer architecture (BatchNorm -> 3 parallel levels of paired 128-neuron ReLU branches -> concat -> per-level 128-neuron dense -> concat -> final 1-neuron dense), Adam lr=0.001 for 1000 epochs on a seeded 405/101 Boston split with train-only z-score normalization. All paper-stated hyperparameters are matched; unstated details (batch size, init scheme, Adam eps, exact data loader) are disclosed reasonable guesses. The reproduced RMSE (3.3292 mean, individual runs 3.7516/2.835/3.4009) brackets the claimed 3.02 within the measured 3-run spread, and the learning curve shows a genuine plateau near the target rather than divergence or under-fitting, consistent with the pass verdict.
curve_assessment:
The eval RMSE (on the script's own monitoring/val split) oscillates between roughly 3.1 and 3.7 from step 80 through step 1000, with best_eval at step 950 reaching 2.9047, i.e. training has plateaued around the target rather than diverging or steadily improving. Train RMSE keeps slowly decreasing (train_metric 1.82 at step 1000, eval_loss 9.834) while eval RMSE does not track it down further, consistent with mild overfitting/variance rather than under-training. The final held-out test RMSE (3.7516 in this run, 3.3292 mean of 3 runs, run values 3.7516/2.835/3.4009) brackets the paper's 3.02 with run-to-run spread comparable to the gap, indicating the reproduction is essentially matching the claim within noise rather than systematically falling short.</curve_assessment>
